dialog.1: Are you the new nursing student starting the assessment practice?
dialog.2: Your mission will be to help me assess the patients assigned to us.
dialog.3: And identify the priority nursing diagnosis according to the patient's needs.
dialog.4: To give you some context, let me explain. Mr. C.J.M, 58 years old, had a stroke 3 months ago.
dialog.5: He is hospitalized due to a urinary infection that is almost resolved with the intravenous pharmacological treatment received.
dialog.6: His companion, who is his wife, says he is only a few days away from leaving the hospital, but she is worried about other needs he has right now.
dialog.7: Come with me to assess the patient, and read the case questions and answers carefully.

question3.question: How do you assess the sensory function of cranial nerve VII?

answers.1: Explore taste on each half of the tongue, in its anterior two thirds.
answers.2: Explore the tongue and whether its two halves are equal and symmetrical.
answers.3: Explore the immediate contraction of the posterior pharyngeal wall.
answers.4: Explore taste in the posterior third of the tongue.

question4.question: Which tests are part of vestibular nerve assessment?

answers.2: Barany pointing deviation test, Romberg maneuver.

question5.question: What characteristics does a normal standing attitude or posture have?

answers.1: Head forward, flat thorax, relaxed abdomen, exaggerated spinal curvatures.
answers.2: Head slightly forward, thorax slightly low, spinal curvatures slightly increased.
answers.3: Adequate alignment of body parts. When the patient faces the nurse at a distance of about 2 m, there is alignment and symmetry of the shoulders, iliac crests, and knees, which should be at the same level. In lateral position, an imaginary line can be drawn through the earlobe, shoulder, hip, femoral trochanter, center of the knee, and in front of the ankle.
answers.4: Head excessively forward, depressed thorax, extremely exaggerated spinal curvatures.

question6.question: Which parts make up the stance phase in the gait cycle?

answers.4: Heel contact, foot flat, mid-stance, terminal stance, toe-off.

powerlessness.definition: Experience of lack of control over a situation, including the perception that one's own actions do not significantly affect the outcome.
powerlessness.evidencedBy:
- Frustration due to inability to perform tasks previously performed.
- Dependence.
- Insufficient sense of control.

anxiety.definition:
Vague and uneasy feeling of discomfort or threat accompanied by an autonomic response, whose origin is often nonspecific or unknown to the person; feeling of apprehension caused by anticipation of danger.
It is an alert signal that warns of imminent danger and allows the person to take measures to face the threat.
anxiety.relatedTo:
- Situational crisis.
- Major changes. (e.g. health status)
anxiety.evidencedBy:
- Irritability.
- Altered attention.
- Confusion.
- Decreased ability to solve problems.
- Decreased perceptual field.
- Concern about changes in life events.

ineffectiveCoping.definition: Inability to make a valid appraisal of stressors, inadequate choices of practiced responses and/or inability to use available resources.
ineffectiveCoping.relatedTo:
- Situational crisis.
- Uncertainty.
- Insufficient sense of control.
ineffectiveCoping.evidencedBy:
- Change in communication pattern.
- Inability to meet basic needs.
- Insufficient problem resolution.

ineffectiveHealthManagement.definition: Pattern of regulation and integration into daily life of a therapeutic regimen for treatment of illness and its sequelae that is unsatisfactory for meeting specific health goals.
ineffectiveHealthManagement.relatedTo:
- Complexity of the therapeutic regimen.
- Excessive demands.
- Powerlessness.
- Perception of severity of condition.
ineffectiveHealthManagement.evidencedBy:
- Does not include treatment regimen in daily life.
- Difficulties with prescribed treatment.

impairedPhysicalMobility.definition: Limitation in independent, purposeful physical movement of the body or of one or more extremities.
impairedPhysicalMobility.relatedTo:
- Neuromuscular impairment.
- Sensoriperceptual impairment.
- Decreased muscle strength.
- Decreased endurance.
- Decreased muscle control.
impairedPhysicalMobility.evidencedBy:
- Alterations in gait.
- Increased reaction time.
- Difficulty turning.
- Discomfort.
- Decreased fine motor skills.
- Decreased gross motor skills.
- Slowed movement.
- Postural instability.
- Limited range of motion.
- Uncoordinated movements.
- Spastic movements.

impairedVerbalCommunication.definition: Decreased, delayed, or absent ability to receive, process, transmit and/or use a symbol system.
impairedVerbalCommunication.relatedTo:
- Central nervous system impairment.
- Altered perception.
impairedVerbalCommunication.evidencedBy:
- Difficulty expressing thoughts verbally (aphasia, apraxia).
- Difficulty forming words (dysarthria).
- Difficulty maintaining communication.
- Disorientation in time.

feedingSelfCareDeficit.definition: Impaired ability to perform or complete feeding activities independently.
feedingSelfCareDeficit.evidencedBy:
- Impaired ability to feed oneself a complete meal.
- Impaired ability to swallow food.

dressingSelfCareDeficit.definition: Impaired ability to perform or complete dressing and grooming activities independently.
dressingSelfCareDeficit.evidencedBy:
- Impaired ability to put on necessary clothing items. (e.g., shirt, socks, shoes).
- Impaired ability to remove necessary clothing items. (e.g., shirt, socks, shoes).
